Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 16, verses 1–2:

Verses 1 to 2

The polytheists of Makkah were in a hurry in this matter. They would say that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) speaks of the destruction of earlier nations, so let the punishment of this world or of the Hereafter come upon us as well. The Prophet (ﷺ) was living in Makkah, and as time passed they pressed this demand more and more. Indeed, they began to mock and went very far in ridicule and derision. They expressed the impression that Muhammad (ﷺ) was frightening them for no reason, and that the threats he gave had no real existence. Therefore they could not believe in mere illusions, nor could they submit before a thing that does not exist. The respite and opportunities which Allah was granting them contained profound wisdom and mercy, but they could not understand it. Moreover, they did not reflect upon the cosmic signs which the Qur'an was presenting, and upon the rational proofs which the Qur'an itself was offering, although these proofs left effects on the heart and sight that could be more effective than frightening with punishment. Allah has blessed man with intellect and understanding; it befits him to reflect upon these proofs. Accepting something merely out of fear belongs only to those people who are weak in the aspect of reason. Frightening also strikes at freedom of will.

In such circumstances He said:

"Itā amrullāh" (16:1), "The command of Allah has come." That is, Allah has decided, His will has turned toward it, and at the time Allah has appointed for its occurrence, these commands, orders and decisions will be issued. Therefore:

"Falā tastaʿjilūhu" (16:1), "So do not seek to hasten it." Allah's decisions are in accordance with His will. Your haste cannot affect His decisions. Your hopes for prolonged respite cannot postpone them either. Whether punishment comes or the Resurrection is established, the decision has been made. The occurrence and execution of this decision will certainly take place at its appointed time. There is no possibility of advancing or delaying it.

However much a person tries to remain firm in his condition, this decisive style of speech affects him nonetheless, even if, out of arrogance, he does not show its effect. Just as the style is decisive, so this reality is also unalterable: when Allah's command comes, it is unalterable. Only it is necessary that Allah's will become connected with a matter, and then that matter comes into being. In the twinkling of an eye it comes into existence. Therefore this forceful manner of speech is not based on any poetic exaggeration. Just as the manner of speech affects the consciousness, so Allah's decisions bring about a real revolution in the actual circumstances.

As for the polytheistic deeds and polytheistic beliefs of the people of Makkah, and all their notions that are based upon polytheistic deeds and beliefs, Allah's Being is free from them.

"Subḥānahū wa taʿālā ʿammā yushrikūn" (16:1), "Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him." Allah is free from all the polytheism in which these people are involved. It should be remembered that a person becomes involved in polytheism only when he has fallen in his thinking and his notions are not based upon any proof.

The commands and orders of Allah have come, which are free from polytheism, and the Lord who gives the command is also free from polytheism, and the station which the people of Makkah assign to Allah is far above it. Therefore Allah does not leave people immersed in their misguided thoughts. Allah sends angels down from the heavens, and these angels bear a message that contains the program for the renewal of human life and for salvation in the Hereafter.

"Yunazzilu al-malāʾikata ... min ʿibādihi" (16:2), "He sends down the angels with the Spirit by His command upon whomever of His servants He wills." This is a very great blessing of Allah. Allah does not send down from the heavens only rain, which provides the means of sustenance for their bodies; rather He also sends down, through the angels, spiritual nourishment for the human being. To call the Qur'an and Islam "the Spirit" is extremely meaningful. The message of the Qur'an revives a society in the same way that a human body is brought to life when a spirit is breathed into it. Through this message the self and conscience come alive, the intellect and consciousness are given polish, and society becomes so alive and healthy that all kinds of corruption are removed from it. Therefore, among the blessings and favours that descend from the heavens for human life, this is the highest and most excellent. This supreme blessing is brought by a creature that is pure in nature, and it descends upon the chosen individuals among Allah's servants, who are the most excellent of mankind; and what is this Spirit? It is the essence of the universe.

"Lā ilāha illā anā fattaqūn" (16:2), "There is no deity except Me, so fear Me."

Allah alone, without partner, is the Sovereign and the Object of worship. This entire belief is the spirit of all beliefs; it is the life of the human self; it is the concept by which society becomes alive and vigorous; and all other concepts apart from it are deadly and destructive for human society. The person who does not believe in the sole Being of Allah is bewildered and distressed, ruined and destroyed. From every direction a false belief pulls him toward itself; concepts based on illusions that contradict one another surround him from all sides, his self is constantly the abode of whisperings, unknown fears and imaginings, and he can never advance in any one direction toward a definite goal. He is surrounded by scattered thoughts and disordered deeds.

To describe Islam as the Spirit is in fact an expression of all these meanings. And at the beginning of the Surah, where Allah mentions all His blessings, to declare Islam the spirit of life means that the Islamic way of life is in truth that supreme blessing, without which a person cannot benefit fully from Allah's other blessings. Indeed the reality is that if this blessing has not been given to someone, then the other favours too lose their value for him, because it is this blessing which truly grants a person everlasting life.

In this verse, warning and admonition are described as the true mission of revelation and prophethood, because all the themes of this Surah revolve around the deniers, the polytheists, and the classes who are ungrateful and deny Allah's blessings. Furthermore, the Surah criticises those who declare the lawful to be unlawful, which is a great crime and a form of polytheism; likewise the Surah criticises those who break their covenant with Allah; and it also discusses those who become apostates after accepting Islam. Therefore, at the beginning of the Surah, to say that people should be warned against these abominable crimes is a fitting opening, in the sense of: O people, be cautious, fear Allah, and be mindful of the Hereafter.

* * *

After this introduction, the proofs and evidences scattered throughout this entire universe, which point to the Oneness of Allah, are presented before people. Then there is mention of some of Allah's blessings, which point to the kindness of the True Benefactor. These signs and blessings are mentioned abundantly and in a continuous stream. The discussion begins with the creation of the heavens and the earth and the creation of the human being.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 16, verses 3–4:

Verses 3 to 4

The same point: the creation of the universe is founded on truth.

{He created the heavens and the earth with truth} (16:3). That is, the fundamental element of their creation is truth. This universe is run in accordance with truth, and the fundamental element and fundamental power that runs this universe and all the creatures within it is truth and reality. Nothing in this universe is in vain, accidental or purposeless. It is established upon truth. It is bound up with truth; it moves towards truth, and its end will also be in accordance with truth.

{Exalted is He above what they associate with Him} (16:3). God is far exalted above the partners that people ascribe to Him. What reason is there for associating with God, who is the Creator of the heavens and the earth, some of His own creatures? Therefore no creature among His creation is fit to be His partner, and so He is the One, without partner.

{He created man from a drop of fluid, and then he becomes an open adversary} (16:4). Look at his beginning, and then after his completion look at his disputatiousness: how immense is the difference! Look at that insignificant and simple drop, and then look at this gentleman who has become a complete disputant and who comes forward against the Creator, who argues with the Creator himself, who denies even the existence of the Creator, or who denies His oneness and assigns partners to Him. Between the state of the drop and the state of contention there is not any great distance of time and space. The Qur'an also adopts such a mode of expression that these distances are erased. The Qur'an shows that the difference between the beginning and the end of man is as great and clear as it is sudden. Thus, in a single moment, two different scenes come before a person: one scene in which man is a worthless drop, and another in which he becomes complete and makes display of his arrogance and stands up in opposition to the Creator Himself. This is both the miraculous quality and the conciseness of this depiction, that is, a miraculous style of expression in the most concise words.

Now let us reflect on the scene of the universe. This is a vast scene: the wide expanse of the heavens and the earth in which Man stands, and around him this whole universe spread out, which has been subjected to man. The discussion begins with the animals that are clearly servants of man.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 16, verses 5–8:

Verses 5 to 8

The society in which the Qur'an was first revealed, namely Makkah Mukarramah, and all such societies that exist even today, especially those whose economy is based on agriculture, cannot even imagine human life without these animals. The animals known in the Arabian Peninsula were these: camels, cows, buffaloes, sheep and goats for eating and drinking, and horses, mules and donkeys for riding and adornment. There is a juristic difference regarding horses. Imam Abu Hanifah (rh) considers their meat unlawful, because some ahadith prohibit it, and also because the Qur'an has mentioned them for riding. The other imams consider it permissible, because authentic ahadith state that eating horse meat is lawful.

The Qur'an presents these animals here as a blessing, because some of them are tied to the material needs of human beings and some are an adornment for human beings. Furthermore, a person makes clothing for himself from their hides, various products are made from their wool and hair, and their milk, meat and so on are used. Ghee, fat and even bones are put to use. These animals carry loads, since a person could transport goods from one place to another by himself, but only with very great hardship. Furthermore, when in the morning you take out your livestock to graze and bring them back in the evening, this is a beauty for you. You are pleased to see them. When they come before your eyes, beautiful and well-fed, returning in the evening full and thriving. Villagers understand the meaning of these verses more deeply than city dwellers. Horses, mules and donkeys are mostly used for carrying loads. They are also made very beautiful for use as mounts.

[Qur'an 16:8] "So that you may ride them and as an adornment" ("li-tarkabuha wa zeenah"): "so that you may ride upon them and they may be a splendour of your life." The word "zeenah" (adornment) deserves particular attention here. Through it, the viewpoint of Islam and the Qur'an on life becomes apparent. From the Islamic perspective, beauty and grace are an essential part of life. The concept of blessing is not limited to the necessities of life, eating, drinking and riding; rather, human pleasure and recreation are also among the necessities of life. The sense of beauty and grace, the awareness of recreation and joy, and refined human taste are, in the view of Islam, more important than mere animal needs and wants.

[Qur'an 16:7] "Indeed your Lord is Kind and Merciful" ("inna rabbakum la-ra'ufun raheem"): This follow-up is upon the fact that if a human being had to do the carrying himself, it would be a task of great hardship. Therefore, the animals that Allah has created for carrying loads are a boundless mercy of Allah and a great blessing.

[Qur'an 16:8] "And He creates what you do not know" ("wa yakhluqu ma la ta'lamoon"): This is a follow-up to the statement that Allah created animals for you, which you eat, use for carrying loads, and which are also a means of adornment, joy and delight. The purpose here is that Allah also creates certain things of which you have no knowledge. Therefore, to reach these purposes, human thinking has been kept open, because in the modern age new means of transport and conveyance also belong to Allah's creations, and you too can create new means of adornment, beautification, recreation and joy. Thus this concept was not restricted to the early society in which the Qur'an was revealed, because Islamic teachings are not confined to time and place. Beyond every age and every time and place there come further ages and further times and places, in which there can be new means of need and joy. People are given the hope that they should expect further creations of Allah. If by Allah's grace a person invents a new convenience or adornment, they should be ready to accept it, and not rise up in opposition to it, nor refuse to benefit from modern discoveries and inventions, saying that our forefathers met their needs only with the animals mentioned above, carrying loads only with horses, mules and donkeys, and therefore we will not use modern means of transport nor benefit from them; or that since the Qur'an has specified only the categories mentioned above, all other conveniences, food and adornments are forbidden. That is why it was said that the scope of creation is vast.

Islam is a worldview that is open and flexible. It benefits from all the powers and capacities of living things, so the Qur'an prepares the minds of Muslims to benefit from the conveniences provided by the powers and sciences of coming ages. A Muslim's mind is so open that he accepts all future discoveries with an Islamic mindset, regards them as among the wonders of Allah and the wonders of knowledge, and considers them a part of life.

In the modern age, new means of carrying, conveyance and transport have come into existence. Along with conveniences, these means are also high sources of beauty and adornment. The people of the Qur'an's revelation era could not even imagine them. Furthermore, in the future there will be means that people of our age cannot think of. For such circumstances the Qur'an prepares people intellectually, so that their minds do not become frozen. This is the meaning of [Qur'an 16:8] "wa yakhluqu ma la ta'lamoon."

The discussion here was that Allah created means of transport for human beings. By using these means, a person covers great distances and reaches from one place to another. In keeping with the subject, Allah also points to spiritual paths and spiritual journeys and their means of conveyance, that there are also ways to Allah. The path to reach Allah is a perfectly straight path. In the world there are also crooked paths that in reality cannot lead to Allah. The path to Allah is shown by Allah Himself. To discover this path, Allah has placed signs in this universe, and they should be reflected upon. That is precisely why some individuals from among humankind have been sent as messengers, so that they too may point out this path.

Now the second part of the verses on creation and blessings.

Verses 10 to 11

This water descends from the heavens according to the laws which Allah has established for this universe. These laws control the movement of the universe. The results of these movements emerge in accordance with the will and planning of the Creator and Sustainer. This rain which falls from the heavens has been described as one of the blessings of Allah.

﴿From it is drink﴾ (16:10), "you drink from it." Its major feature is that it quenches thirst. After this, its next feature:

﴿And from it are trees in which you pasture your livestock﴾ (16:10). All pastures and the leaves of trees fall under this heading. Pastures and trees have been mentioned in relation to animals, for whom fodder is thus provided. Then the mention of agricultural produce, which serves as food for humans, follows. Further, regarding human food, a variety of fruits such as olives, dates, grapes and others are mentioned.

﴿Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought﴾ (16:11). On what matter should one reflect? On how Allah manages this universe with such great wisdom. He has set in motion within it such unchanging laws of nature which sustain human life. Man could never have survived on this earth, or this star of the universe called Earth, had Allah not established within the universe such laws of nature which sustain life for him, which are in harmony with his nature, and which fulfil his natural desires. It is not mere coincidence that man was created on this earth, that this earth was placed in its present relationship with the other celestial bodies, and that atmospheric and cosmic movements were determined by mere chance in the system they are in today, and that by mere chance they became conducive to human life in the way we see them.

Those who have the capacity for reflection understand the wise planning and wise management of Allah. Those who study the earth connect the characteristics of vegetation, its fruits and flowers, and the system of winds and rains to the laws of nature of Allah, and draw the conclusion that there is one wise Creator who did all of this. He is One, without partner. His will is one and the same, and the effects and fruits of His laws are uniform. As for the heedless, they see these things morning and evening, in summer and in winter, yet their faculties of understanding remain asleep. Their faculties of perception and their conscience and consciousness do not set out in search of the Wise One who created this diverse universe. They do not consider who is the originator of this wondrous and strange system.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 16, verse 12:

Now the third group of signs of the universe.

Verse 12

The alternation of night and day is one manifestation of God's governance of creation and of His blessings upon man. The movement of the sun and moon, and this system of planets and stars, also serves as a means of sustenance for human life. All these phenomena are engaged in the service of human beings; from the day of their creation they have been assigned to this service. The alternation of night and day has a decisive effect on human life. Just consider: what if the day were to remain perpetual and the night never came, or the night were to remain perpetual and the day never came? In the first case the earth would burn, and in the second case the earth would freeze.

The connection of the sun and moon with the system of life on this earth is entirely clear. Human life is directly linked to the movement of the sun and moon.

﴿And the stars are subjected by His command﴾ (16:12): "all the stars are subjected by His command." These are all beneficial and sustaining for human and non-human creatures, and the true knowledge of their benefits belongs to Allah alone. These matters are a part of Allah's wisdom and governance, and all of Allah's governing laws are in harmony with one another. Only those people can understand these governing laws and the wisdom of this governance who reflect and realize that behind the phenomena of nature there is a governing power at work.

﴿Indeed, in that are signs for a people who use reason﴾ (16:12): "in this there are many signs for those people who use their intellect."

Now comes the fourth group of signs and proofs in the universe:

Verse 13

God created the earth and brought forth within it various kinds of minerals, stones of many colours and other things upon which human life depends. Yet God has created stores of these necessities of life that never run out. Moreover, the new discoveries that man keeps making in this earth, and the hidden treasures and sources of power within the earth that he keeps uncovering, continue to increase as his needs and requirements grow. As one treasure is exhausted, several more sources of power are discovered. This is the provision of God, which He has stored up for His servants.

﴿Indeed in that is a sign for a people who remember﴾ (16:13). Such people do not forget that the hand of divine power has deposited these treasures for us.

Now comes the fifth group of signs and proofs in the universe, concerning the diverse creatures with which the bitter sea is filled. The sea's water is not fit for drinking, yet it is beneficial to man in many respects.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 16, verse 14:

Verse No. 14

The varied life of the seas is also beneficial and useful for human life. The seas also contain other means for human enjoyment and interest. Fish and other sea creatures are excellent food for people. Moreover, pearls, coral and oysters from the sea still serve humanity as adornments, even in today's modern age. Here, the benefit of the ship is mentioned not only as a means of travel, but also attention is drawn to the beauty of the scene of ships moving across the seas.

﴿وَتَرَى الْفُلْكَ مَوَاخِرَ فِيهِ﴾ (16:14) "You see the ship cutting through the chest of the sea." By the word "tara" (you see), attention is drawn to the beautiful scene of the ship, the water and the movement of the ship. We see sea vessels cutting through the water as they go. This phrase once again points to the reality that Islam does not overlook the aesthetic aspect of this world. Everything in the universe has been made beautiful for human beings in addition to being useful for life.

Then the Qur'an, through this scene, teaches people the lesson that it is useful for you, a means of your travel and trade, and this scene is also beautiful to your eyes; but all these things also require that you give thanks to Allah.

﴿وَلِتَبْتَغُوا مِن فَضْلِهِ وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ﴾ (16:14) "All this is so that you may seek His bounty and become grateful to Him."

Now we come to the last group of signs and proofs in the cosmos in this lesson.

Verses 15 to 16

He placed mountains on the earth as stakes. Modern geography discusses the causes of this, but modern science has not explained that if there were no mountains, the earth would tilt to one side.

This fact has been stated only by the Holy Quran. Modern geography gives causes for the existence of mountains that are contrary to this. For example, it says that the interior of the earth is hot lava, and when it cools it contracts, and the earth's surface above it also contracts and takes the form of a fold, which is a mountain. In this way, high mountains and valleys come into existence. But the Holy Quran says that these mountains create a balance of movement within the earth. Modern science has perhaps not yet considered this aspect.

Opposite these mountains are great valleys, and within them various paths, streams and brooks. Attention is also drawn to this. Rivers and streams have a natural connection with mountains. Rivers flow out of mountains. Snow falls on the mountains and rain falls, and from this the rivers and streams and their routes come into being. Then people travel on these routes, transport goods and carry loads. Then landmarks for these routes are set up, just as these mountains serve as signposts for paths; in the same way, in deserts and seas, the stars serve as guides. In short, this entire universe of Allah is beneficial for humanity.

After the explanation of the creation, the signs, the bounties of Allah, and the wisdom in the management of the cosmos, now the matter for which all these proofs and evidences were presented is clearly stated. All these evidences were brought for the purpose that Allah is One, without partner, and that He is exalted above what these people associate with Him as partners.

The commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 16, verses 17–21:

Verses 17 to 21

And those other beings whom people call upon besides Allah create nothing, but are themselves created. They are dead, not living, and they do not know when they will be raised up (again to life).

This conclusion is drawn at a most fitting moment, in circumstances where the human self and sound reason are ready to accept its content.

﴿Is He who creates like one who does not create? Will you not then take heed?﴾ (16:17). The answer is simply: certainly not. Can any sensitive and reflective person consider the Being of majesty and attributes, who has created this magnificent universe, to be equal to one who has created nothing at all, neither great nor small?

﴿Will you not then take heed?﴾ (16:17). For this, only a refreshing of memory is needed; this matter is already present within your nature.

After mentioning the many colours and aspects of His favours, Allah said:

﴿And if you were to count the favours of Allah, you could not enumerate them﴾ (16:18). Giving thanks for them is far beyond reach, because neither can they be counted nor can thanks be fully rendered. Rather, most of Allah's favours are such that man still has no knowledge of them, because some matters man regards as routine and is not even conscious of them. He becomes aware only when a favour is taken away. Just consider the mechanism of the human body, each part of which performs a duty, and a person feels its worth only when some part of the body becomes useless. Then he realises how great a blessing he has been deprived of. Indeed, the attribute of Allah's mercy and His attribute of pardon reach the one who falls short and the weak who need help.

﴿Indeed Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful﴾ (16:18). He is the Creator, a Being who knows all our open and hidden affairs.

﴿And Allah knows what you conceal and what you disclose﴾ (16:19). Therefore it is astonishing that people equate Allah with those beings and things which can create not even the smallest thing, know nothing, and are in fact dead; life can never enter into them, and for this reason they have no consciousness.

﴿And those whom they call upon besides Allah create nothing, and they are themselves created. They are dead, not living, and they do not know when they will be raised up﴾ (16:20–21). The reference here to resurrection after death means that the one who is a Creator must have knowledge of resurrection, because the completion of creation will be when the Last Day comes, and then all rational beings will be recompensed for their deeds with reward and punishment. Therefore gods who have no knowledge of resurrection after death are not fit to be deities or worshipped. It is a mockery that a creator should not know his creation, nor know when that creation will be raised.

**Lesson 120: At a Glance**

In the previous lesson we were told that this great creation of the Creator of the universe contains countless signs and indications. In this great creation there are only benefits for mankind, and the true Creator knows the outward and inward state of human beings. Those beings and things that you regard as gods have no creation of their own. They are themselves created; they have no knowledge or awareness of anything. Rather, they are dead, and life cannot be granted to them in this world now, or they are not even fit for life. Moreover, these beings do not even know when they will be raised for reckoning and recompense. All these arguments decisively establish that these beings are not worthy of worship, and that the belief in association (shirk) is entirely false and futile. In this surah, this was the first phase of the exposition of the doctrine of tawhid, in which there was also a reference to the Establishment of the Hour (qiyamah).

This lesson also contains the subject that we left in the previous lesson. This is the second phase of the exposition of tawhid, and it begins with the claim that your god is only one God. Those who do not accept the one God alone, in reality, have denying hearts. Since denial is seated in their hearts, they do not acknowledge the truth despite the abundant evidence of this universe. Along with the seating of denial in their hearts, these people are afflicted with the disease of arrogance and pride, and this pride also prevents them from accepting the truth. This theme concludes with an impressive scene: in this universe, all shadows in reality prostrate before the Great Majesty. All the animals of this universe also prostrate before Allah. The angels too bow before the One God, whose essence is free of arrogance and whose hearts are free of fear, and they carry out Allah's commands at all times without any hesitation or questioning. These displays of obedience are presented in contrast to the arrogance of the arrogant ones mentioned at the beginning of this lesson.

Between the beginning and the end of this lesson, the Qur'an also places before the reader the viewpoint of these arrogant ones, namely what their position is: they say that the revelation and the Qur'an are ancient tales, and they ask why they associate partners with Allah, and why they declare forbidden things that Allah has not forbidden. They say that it is Allah's will, and that if Allah had not willed it, they could never have done so. Regarding the Hereafter, their position is that they swear solemn oaths that Allah will never resurrect the dead. All these assumptions of theirs are strongly refuted in this lesson, and the manner of the refutation is that when they are raised on the Day of Resurrection, they themselves will plainly deny these views of theirs. Alongside this, some events of the destroyed nations are presented as examples, and they are warned that the punishment may come upon them in some hour of the day or night in the same way, when they have no expectation of it, and in some forms they may anticipate the punishment and be waiting for it. In contrast, a glimpse of the position and views of the believers is also shown in this lesson, especially their dialogue with the angels at the time of death and at resurrection after death. The lesson thus concludes, containing scenes of humility, submission, and obedience to the command of God, as well as scenes of denial. The whole universe, its shadows, the angels, the alternation of night and day, and the heavens and the earth, all are signs of compliance with the command of God.

**Verses 22–23**

Translation: Here, faith in Allah as the One and faith in the Last Day are united. Indeed, faith in the Last Day is made the necessary consequence of faith in the One Allah, because the worship of the One Allah is directly connected with the belief in the Hereafter and the establishment of reward and punishment. Only in this way can the wisdom of the true Creator in creation be manifested and complete justice be done.

﴿Your God is only one God﴾ (16:22). The signs of creation that were enumerated in this surah, the blessings of Allah that were mentioned, and the matters of Allah's knowledge and wisdom that were described, all demand this great truth: that Allah is one. His traces are manifest in the laws of power and the natural order of this universe, and complete harmony, mutual cooperation, and conformity are found among them, and all these laws proceed in unison.

Therefore, those who do not accept this truth do not accept the Hereafter. Those who believe in Allah's creation, His oneness, His wisdom, and His justice, the necessary consequence is that they then believe in the Establishment of the Hour. If they do not do so, the cause is not a lack of arguments and signs such that they do not do so; rather, the cause of denial is hidden within their own selves. Denial is in their disposition, and their hearts are deniers. Denial is already settled in their minds and hearts. Therefore they do not pay attention to arguments and proofs. And why do they not pay attention to arguments and proofs? Because they are arrogant and consider themselves to be something great. They accept neither the arguments nor the leadership of the Prophet (ﷺ). In truth, these people do not want to worship Allah. Therefore they deny, and the real cause lies within their own selves.

Allah, who created all of mankind, knows every part of His creation. He knows what is hidden and what is apparent, and without doubt He knows everything, and He also dislikes their conduct.

﴿Indeed, He does not love the arrogant﴾ (16:23). It cannot be expected that an arrogant heart will be satisfied with the arguments and evidences of this universe and bow in submission. Therefore they are people disliked by Allah, because they are afflicted with pride of self, and Allah knows well their circumstances and reality, and He knows every outward and inward state of theirs.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 16, verses 24–25:

Verses 24 to 25

When these arrogant people, whose hearts deny, are asked, "Mā dhā anzala rabbukum" (16:24), "What has your Lord sent down?", they do not give a correct answer. Yet the answer is simple and straightforward. These people can read the Qur'an and can understand its meaning. Even if they do not believe, they could still give an honest and correct answer. But instead of answering directly, they said:

"Asāṭīr al-awwalīn" (16:24), "They are merely the tales of the ancients." Asāṭīr (myths, fables) is the term for stories that are full of illusion and filled with superstition. These people make such remarks about the Qur'an, although the Qur'an offers a most reasonable critique and genuine guidance concerning human reason, human psychology, human ways of life, the general conduct of people, the relationship between the classes of society, and the past, present and future of man. The Qur'an has related the accounts of earlier nations, so their opinion of it is a superficial one. Thus these people increase the burden of their own sins, and also take on a share of the sins of their followers, because their followers are led astray by their words and turn away from Islam and faith. Since these followers are themselves ignorant, they are unable to form any correct opinion on their own. The Qur'an describes the sins of these people by the image of a load carried by a traveler. The load is heavy, yet this foolish traveler keeps adding to it more and more. This burden bends the human soul and subjects it to such hardship as a heavy load bends the back double. In truth, a spiritual and psychological burden causes a person the same exhaustion that a physical burden causes the body; indeed, the psychological burden crushes the body far more than a physical burden does.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrates from al-Suddi that the Quraysh held a meeting and decided that Muhammad (ﷺ) had a sweet tongue; when he speaks to someone, that person's reason is lost. Therefore, they said, choose from among the Quraysh a few persons who are well known and whose lineage is well known, and seat them on the roads of Makkah for a night or two, so that whoever comes to meet Muhammad (ﷺ) they may turn back. Accordingly, some people set out and sat down on the road to Makkah. Whoever came to Makkah from his people to find out about Muhammad's (ﷺ) circumstances, the person sitting on the road among them would say, "I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so." This man would recognize him, because he was a famous person. Then he would say, "I will tell you about Muhammad (ﷺ). He is a great liar. Those who follow him in this matter are either foolish people or slaves who have no standing. As for the elders and chiefs of his people, they are all opposed to him." In this way, the visitor would listen to the words of a respected man and turn back. Upon this, this verse was revealed:

"Wa idhā qīla lahum..." to "Asāṭīr al-awwalīn" (16:24): "And when it is said to them, 'What has your Lord sent down?', they say, 'Tales of the ancients.'" Now, if this man had been a person of firm resolve, and if guidance had been written for him, then when these people spoke of their own affairs he would have said, "How useless a representative of my people I would be: I have traveled a long distance, and only one day's journey remains, and now I should return without meeting this man, without seeing what he says, and without bringing back to my people any verified account." Such a man would have entered Makkah, met the believers, and asked what the teachings of Muhammad (ﷺ) were, and they would have told him good things.

The Quraysh had launched a massive campaign of hostile propaganda against the Islamic movement. After the Quraysh, in every age and place, arrogant people likewise run such hostile campaigns against the Islamic movement, because their pride and arrogance prevent them from following proof and truth. Thus these arrogant people of Quraysh were, at the outset, deniers and hostile opponents. The Qur'an clearly presents before them the end of the arrogant people who came before them, especially the fate that awaits them on the Day of Resurrection; indeed, this end of theirs will begin even before the Resurrection, as soon as their souls leave their earthly bodies. The Qur'an presents these scenes before them in a most forceful manner, as is its style.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 16, verses 26–29:

Verses 26 to 29

﴿Qad makara alladhina min qablihim﴾ (16:26) "Those before them also devised schemes (to bring down the truth)." The Qur'an describes their propaganda as a building that has foundations, pillars and a roof. The purpose is to show that their propaganda was deep, strong, firm and massive, but it did not succeed against the power and plan of Allah.

﴿Fa-atallahu bunyanahum min al-qawa'id fa-kharra 'alayhim al-saqf min fawqihim﴾ (16:26) "So Allah struck at their building from its foundations, and the roof fell upon them from above them." This is a picture that brings the scene of complete destruction before the eyes. The destruction comes both from above and from below, because the very foundations on which this building stood collapsed, and the roof fell upon them in such a way that they were buried and sunk beneath it.

﴿Wa atahumu al-'adhabu min haythu la yash'urun﴾ (16:26) "And punishment came upon them from a direction they did not expect." We see that the building they had constructed with such firmness, and in which they had complete confidence that they would find refuge, became their tomb, and it brought upon them such destruction that ruin came upon them from above and from below. They had built it so strongly that they had no fear of destruction from any side.

This is a complete scene of ruin and destruction. It is a meaningful mockery of the schemes of those who devise plots and hostile strategies. Those who plot to block the path of the Islamic movement think that their schemes will have no counter and that their plans will not fail, while Allah encompasses all their deceptions and plans.

This scene has been seen in the era of the Quraysh. It has been seen in history many times before them and in later periods too. The call of Islam continues its journey to this day. Let the plotters devise as much as they wish and practise as much deception as they wish. The workers of the Islamic movement read these historical scenes again and again, just as the Qur'an depicted them.

﴿Fa-atallahu bunyanahum ... la yash'urun﴾ (16:26) "So behold, Allah struck at their building from its foundations, the roof fell upon them from above, and punishment came upon them from a direction they did not expect." This was their end in this world and on this earth.

﴿Thumma yawma al-qiyamati yukhzihim wa yaqulu ayna shuraka'iya alladhina kuntum tushaqqunna fihim﴾ (16:27) "Then on the Day of Resurrection He will disgrace them and say, 'Where are My partners, concerning whom you used to dispute with the people of truth?'" Here the Qur'an depicts a scene of the Resurrection. These arrogant schemers are in a state of great shame in this scene. Their pride has evaporated and the days of their deceptions have passed. Now they stand in the court of that Mighty Lord who owns creation and whose decisions alone prevail. Allah now asks them so as to shame and disgrace them further.

﴿Ayna shuraka'iya alladhina kuntum tushaqqunna fihim﴾ (16:27) "Where are My partners about whom you used to dispute?" The false partners about whom you used to argue with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers, where are they? You used to hold debates with those who held to the belief in Tawhid.

Here these people stand silent and bewildered, drowned in shame. But the angels, the messengers, the people of knowledge and the believers will now be permitted to speak, for they will then have prevailed, and so speaking will be their right.

﴿Qala alladhina utu al-'ilma inna al-khizya al-yawma wa al-su'a 'ala al-kafirin﴾ (16:27) "Those who were given knowledge will say, 'Indeed, today disgrace and misfortune are upon the disbelievers.'" In truth, today disgrace and misfortune belong only to the disbelievers.

﴿Alladhina tatawaffahumu al-malaikatu zalimi anfusihim﴾ (16:28) "Those whom the angels take in death while they wrong themselves." Now the Qur'an takes these people one step back: before the Resurrection, the time of their death has drawn near. The angels seize their souls, and the soul is drawn out of their bodies with great harshness, because these people were deprived of faith and certainty. They had cast their own souls into destruction. Then their lives were handed over to the punishment of the Fire and of eternity.

When the death of these people drew near, while they were still engaged in the business of falsehood, deceit and trickery on earth, behold how humbled they have become.

﴿Fa-alqaw al-salama ma kunna na'malu min su'in﴾ (16:28) "Then they will throw down their submission and say, 'We were not doing any evil.'" These arrogant ones now present themselves as messengers of peace; they offer submission and obedience. This too is a lie, and it is part of their worldly chain of falsehood. They say this with great humility.

﴿Ma kunna na'malu min su'in﴾ (16:28) "We were not doing any evil." This too is a scene of extreme shame and humiliation. Look at these arrogant ones, and look at their condition.

But the answer will come from Allah: "Yes," and this answer will come from the All-Knowing, All-Aware.

﴿Bala inna Allaha 'alimun bima kuntum ta'malun﴾ (16:28) "Yes, Allah is well aware of what you used to do." Therefore falsehood, deception and camouflage can no longer work here.

Now comes the time of their judgment and recompense. This is the recompense of the arrogant.

﴿Fa-udkhulu abwaba jahannama khalidina fiha fa-labi'sa mathwa al-mutakabbirin﴾ (16:29) "Now enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein forever. Indeed, how wretched is the abode of the arrogant." Now the opposing party is those who adopted the path of piety. These people stand in opposition to the arrogant and the proud, from beginning to end.

﴿Beneath which rivers flow,﴾ (16:31) there will be many comforts.

Now, the new argument presented by the polytheists in defense of their shirk and their practices.

Verses 35 to 36

The summary of this new argument of these people is that they attribute their shirk, their worship of idols, the shirk and idol-worship of their forefathers, and the act of making some lawful things unlawful to the will and volition of Allah. They say: if Allah had willed and it had not been His intention, then neither would we have done these acts contrary to the Shariah, nor would our forefathers have done so. If Allah did not will it, when would all these deeds have come about?

In reality, these people have not understood the concept of divine will (mashi'ah). They wish to snatch away from humankind two important distinguishing qualities that Allah has bestowed upon man.

Allah does not desire for His servants that they commit shirk, nor is it His pleasure that what He has made lawful as good things be wrongfully made unlawful. Allah's pleasure is established in all the laws of the Shariah and in the guidance of all the prophets. All the messengers conveyed this, strove for it, and fully discharged the duty of calling to the religion.

Wa-laqad ba'athna... al-taghut (16:36): "We sent a messenger to every nation, (saying), 'Worship Allah and shun the taghut'." This is Allah's command and this is His will concerning His creation. Allah does not, in any case, prevent people from acts over which, in terms of creation, they have the power to refrain. Nor has Allah compelled people to oppose Him, and the proof of this is that when people oppose Allah's commands, He seizes them and punishes them.

Fa-siru fi al-ardi fa-nzuru kayfa kana 'aqibatu al-mukadhdhibin (16:36): "So travel through the earth and see what was the end of those who denied." The requirement of Allah's will is that He created man with the capacity for both guidance and misguidance, and that man has the choice to freely adopt whichever path he wishes. Then Allah gave man intellect so that, by employing his intellect, he might choose one of these two paths for himself. Moreover, for the intellect, Allah has placed in this universe such proofs and evidences which invite the eye, ear, intellect, consciousness, heart and mind of man to reflection, and he sees these proofs and evidences day and night. Then Allah did not rest content with man choosing the right path for himself solely by the strength of his intellect and consciousness. Allah sent a messenger for every era and every nation, so that if a difficult matter becomes hard for human reason to decide, the messenger may present before humankind, in the form of a Shariah, a standard of good and evil in detail, so that man's personal desires and inclinations cannot mislead him. Then Allah did not make these messengers compelling and forceful such that they would twist people's necks and throw them onto the path of faith. He made them only conveyers, so that through preaching and admonition they might turn people towards the right path, and tell them: worship Allah alone, and worship none other than Allah, neither idols, nor their own whims and desires, nor any king.

Wa-laqad ba'athna... wa-ijtanibu al-taghut (16:36): "We sent a messenger to every nation, (saying), 'Worship Allah and shun the taghut'." Thereupon one group accepted this call.

Faminhum man hada Allah (16:36): "Then among them Allah guided some."

And some adopted the path of misguidance.

Wa-minhum man haqqat 'alayhi al-dalalah (16:36): "And upon some, misguidance was imposed."

Verse 37

The determining factor of guidance and misguidance does not depend on whether the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is eager for it or not, since the duty of the Messenger is only to convey (the message). As for guidance and misguidance, they are bestowed in accordance with the Sunnah of Allah (sunnat-ilahiyyah, the divine way or law), and this Sunnah is such that its results cannot be prevented. The Third Obstinate Objection of the Deniers and Arrogant Ones

Verses 38–40

Since God sent His Messengers and they warned of resurrection after death, and the work of enjoining good and forbidding evil began, most people have remained in doubt about the belief in resurrection after death. The people of Quraysh too would swear by God with the most emphatic oaths that God would never raise anyone up again after death. These people acknowledged the existence of God, but they did not believe that God would raise the dead from their graves in their original state. They thought that this task was very difficult: when a person decays and turns to dust particle by particle, how could it be gathered together again?

But these people did not reflect on how God had first given life to those particles. They could not even properly understand the power of God, and they measured the power of God by human power. Nothing is difficult for God to create. When God wills something, He says "Be," and it is.

Moreover, they did not consider what the wisdom of resurrection after death is. Countless matters in this world do not reach their natural conclusion. In this world there is intense disagreement among people about truth and falsehood. People's conceptions of guidance and misguidance differ. The standard of good and evil varies. God does not settle these matters among people in this world, because His will required that people be given respite and distinction in this world, and that not everyone be rewarded or punished right here. These matters will be decided on the Day of Resurrection, at the time of resurrection after death.

The Quran refutes this disbelieving obstinacy at the very outset, and God removes this error and wrong thinking by saying: ﴿It is a promise binding upon Him, a truth﴾ (16:38). And when God resolves upon something, its violation never occurs under any circumstance.

﴿But most people do not know﴾ (16:38), namely what the reality of God's promise is, that it is inviolable.

Then, behind God's decision there is also a profound wisdom.

﴿That He may make clear to them that about which they differ, and that those who disbelieve may know that they were liars﴾ (16:39). Such a thing is necessary so that God may reveal to them the reality about which they are disputing, and so that the deniers of truth may learn that they were liars. In what? In their claim that they are upon guidance, in their claim that they considered the Messenger a liar, and in their claim that the Establishment of the Hour is impossible for them. And also in their deeds, beliefs, and so forth.

As for its actual establishment, it is no difficulty at all.

﴿Indeed, Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, "Be," and it is﴾ (16:40). We need do nothing more to bring a thing into existence than command it, "Be," and it is. The Establishment of the Hour is also one of these states: the moment the will of God turns toward it, it will come to pass.

In contrast to the deniers and the rejecters, here is a glimpse of the truthful believers, who not only hold firm faith in their way of life but also leave their wealth and homeland and migrate for its sake, and they do this solely for the pleasure of Allah.

Moreover, they did not leave their wealth and homeland willingly, but abandoned them out of distress caused by oppression. If they left behind good dwellings here, then it is necessary that in this world they should also be granted circumstances better than those conditions.

﴿Lanubawwiannahum fid-dunya hasanah﴾ (16:41): "We will surely settle them in a good place in this world." And in the Hereafter too We will lodge them in excellent abodes. ﴿Wa la-ajrul-akhirati akbar﴾ (16:41): "And the reward of the Hereafter is surely greater." Would that people knew this.

﴿Alladhina sabaru wa 'ala Rabbihim yatawakkalun﴾ (16:42): "Those who were patient and who put their trust in their Lord." They do not associate anything with Allah; they rely upon Him alone and turn towards Him. If there were no Resurrection, where would such people receive their reward?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah an-Nahl (16), verses 45–50:

Verses 45–50

It is most striking that the hand of divine power can be seen at work within human society. Some people fall into the severe grip of Allah. They keep on scheming and devising plans, but when the seizure of Allah comes, it is the grip of a dominant and powerful Being. Then their strength, their wealth and their vast knowledge cannot save them. Yet despite this, the rest of the schemers continue their intrigues, and those who escape the punishments of Allah go on living as though nothing had happened at all. Except that this cannot happen to them. They do not fear that God might seize them too. At every moment they are within reach of Allah's grip, whether they are asleep or awake, heedless or alert. The Qur'an awakens human feeling and human intuition so that people may fear the expected punishment, and it is only those who are losers who are heedless of the punishment of Allah.

﴿Do those who devise evil plans feel secure that Allah will not cause the earth to swallow them, or that the punishment will not come upon them from a direction they do not perceive?﴾ (16:45). Or that Allah will not seize them while they are going about in towns and villages, engaged in trade and travel.

﴿And they cannot escape⁠—﴾ (16:46). Their being seized, or the place of their capture, is in no way beyond Allah's reach.

﴿Or He seizes them while they are in a state of dread﴾ (16:47). For their being watchful and expecting punishment cannot in any way repel the punishment of Allah. Allah can seize them when they are prepared to defend themselves, and also when they are heedless. But Allah is most Kind and Merciful.

Do these people, who keep thinking of evil schemes, feel secure from the punishment of Allah? Why do they remain bewildered in their deceit? Why do these people keep advancing in their misguidance without returning, and not fear God? Despite the fact that the universe spread around them is calling out with its laws of nature and norms of divine power that this is the path of faith. Rather, this whole universe is a guide and a witness to the Being of the Creator.

﴿Have they not considered the things that Allah has created, how their shadows turn about the right and the left, prostrating themselves to Allah, and they are humbled?﴾ (16:48).

The spectacle of the movements of shadows! The shadow advances, recedes, and then comes to rest in one place. This is a scene that invites only the eye that is open to contemplate it, gives admonition to the heart whose doors are open, gives awareness to the sense that is awake, and guides the person whose faculties of perception move in step with the universe.

Here the Qur'an describes the obedience to the laws of nature and the ordinances of creation as prostration. Prostration is the final picture of humility and submissiveness. Attention is drawn here to the fact that the shadows of trees lengthen and then shrink. The movement of a shadow is extremely subtle, yet its effect on human consciousness is profoundly deep. Then, along with this cosmic creation, the host of angels, objects, trees, shadows, birds and animals, and then the angels, all of them prostrate before Allah in humility and submission and perform worship and servitude! They neither act arrogantly against Allah's servitude nor deviate even a hair's breadth. They do not refuse Allah's commands. But O denier from among the children of Adam, how hard-hearted you are, that you are both arrogant and disobedient. This is your most astonishing conduct!

This lesson ends here by pointing toward the deniers and the arrogant, so that at the end of the lesson it addresses them particularly: your denial and arrogance are contrary to the nature of the universe.

Lesson No. 121: At a Glance

This is the third stage of the issue of Tawhid (Oneness of God), the meaning of which is that the God of this universe is one God alone. This lesson begins with the concept that Allah is One, who alone is the Owner and the Bestower of blessings. The first three verses express this very meaning. Here an excellent parable is given: there is one owner, a provider, and another person who is a slave, a possession, and dependent, who has no authority and over whose property nothing rests. Can these two be equal? Then how can Allah, who is the Creator, Owner and Provider, and your appointed partners, who are neither owners nor providers, be equal? How can we say of both that they are gods, and this one too!

In this lesson, a model of people is also presented: when they fall into some calamity, they call upon Allah alone, but when the calamity is removed, they again begin to commit shirk.

In this lesson, several forms of the superstitions and myths of idol worship are also given. These people set aside certain animals for their made-up gods, although their own condition is that they are unwilling to give any of their possessions into the authority of their slaves, nor are they ready to share anything with them. They themselves greatly dislike daughters, yet they call the angels the daughters of Allah.

﴿Wa-idha bushshira ahaduhum bil-untha zalla wajhuhu muswaddan wa-huwa kazim﴾ (16:57): "And when one of them is given the good news of a female child, his face becomes dark and he is greatly distressed." These people attribute to Allah what they themselves dislike, yet their tongues constantly claim that good is destined for them and that whatever they are doing will end well. These superstitions and myths have come down to them as an inheritance from their forefathers, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sent precisely to explain their reality openly before them. Therefore he (ﷺ) is a guide and a mercy for the believers.

After this, some things created by the true God are given as examples, and if a person reflects on them even a little, he can gain much admonition and lesson, because the creation of these things is possible only for the One alone, and these things are proofs of Allah's divinity and His supremacy. For instance, that Allah arranged for rain to descend from the heavens, by which dead land becomes green and fresh. Then Allah produced, apart from water, very wholesome and delicious milk for people to drink, and this milk comes forth from between the dung and the blood of the animal. Then Allah produced dates and grapes; you make intoxicants from them and also good provision. Then He revealed to the honeybee: make your homes in the mountains, in the trees, and in the trellises that people erect, and from it comes honey, in which there is healing for people. Allah created people; some He takes quickly, and others live to a great age, so that they forget knowledge and become so simple that they know nothing. Then Allah gave some people preference over others in provision. Then He gave some wives, sons and grandsons. Despite these realities, some people worship partners who have no power to provide any sustenance to people in the heavens and the earth, and along with this they make others equal and similar to Allah.

These proofs, which are scattered in the human self and its environment, the Qur'an directs man towards them, so that they may perceive the power of Allah, which is active in their being, their provision, their food, their drink, and in every thing around them that benefits them. The lesson concludes again with the two examples to which we have pointed. This is, as it were, a useful effort to awaken human reason and intuition, which has profound effects, and in it the most sensitive strings of the human soul's instrument have been touched; therefore it is not possible that the human soul should not be affected by it and not respond.

Verses 51 to 55

It is the command of Allah: do not take two gods. God is only One. The style adopted for this statement is very decisive and affirmative. After "Allah" the word "two" comes, and in the second clause there is an emphatic phrase that "Allah is only One," and after these two clauses there is another phrase: "So fear Me alone." And do not fear anyone besides Me; do not adopt toward anyone else the same conduct of fear that is due to Me. The word "fa-rhabun" is used so that you fear Me most of all. In the Islamic view of life, the doctrine of Tawhid is a fundamental matter. The Islamic view of life is established precisely upon the doctrine of Tawhid. Without Tawhid, faith cannot be established, and without faith, the Islamic view of life cannot be established. Therefore this matter must be so clear in the mind and heart of a person that there is no ambiguity in it and no complication.

And when the Creator, Owner and God is He alone, then the owner of this earth, the heavens and the universe is also He alone:

﴿Wa-lahu ma fis-samawati wal-ard﴾ (16:52): "To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth."

﴿Wa-lahud-din wasiba﴾ (16:52): "And to Him belongs religion perpetually." That is, since these universes and religion came into existence, the religion of Him has been continuously in operation, and the Bestower of favours is also Allah alone.

﴿Wa-ma bikum min ni'matin fa-minallah﴾ (16:53): "Whatever blessing you have is from Allah." This matter is placed within your nature: when a difficult time comes, your nature cries out that you should call upon Him alone. In that difficult time, no imaginary helper or idol remains in a person's memory.

﴿Thumma idha massakumud-durru fa-ilayhi taj'arun﴾ (16:53): "Then when a hard time befalls you, to Him you hasten with your cries." At that time you again cry out loudly, asking Him to rescue you from this difficulty. Thus the Qur'an establishes Allah as the sole source of divinity, sovereignty, dominion, legislation, blessing, guidance and the system of life. Human nature confirms this in that when a person is seized by a great calamity, his true nature becomes purified of all the stains and impurities of shirk. Yet some people are still so perverse that when this terrible danger passes from them, they suddenly begin to commit shirk. Thus they are ungrateful for Allah's bounties and turn away from His guidance. But this brief period of the world will soon end, and wait, for they will be afflicted with calamity in the Hereafter.

﴿Fa-tamatta'u fa-sawfa ta'lamun﴾ (16:55): "So enjoy yourselves; soon you will know." This is the model of creatures whose features the Qur'an has drawn here.

﴿Thumma idha massakumud-durru ... yushrikun﴾ (16:54): "Then when a hard time befalls you, you hasten to Him with your cries. But when Allah removes that time, suddenly a group among you begins to associate others with their Lord." People of this kind are always found among mankind. In difficulties, hearts turn to Allah, because by the demands of nature man knows that there is no saviour except Allah. In times of well-being, man is immersed in luxury and ease, so his bond with Allah weakens. In this there are many kinds of deviation, and the greatest of these deviations is associating partners with Allah; moreover, man also grants divine status to certain customs and values, although he does not call them gods.

Sometimes his deviation becomes very severe and his nature is completely corrupted, so that some people, even in the most extreme circumstances, do not call upon Allah, but call upon other beings for protection, rescue and help. Their excuse is that these beings have standing and rank with Allah, and sometimes people call upon other beings besides this notion, for example some people call upon the saints of Allah in times of calamity. This conduct of theirs is worse than the shirk of the pagans of the age of ignorance, because concerning the pagans of the age of ignorance the Qur'an says that in severe difficulties they called upon Allah alone.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 16, verse 56:

For example, these people declare certain animals forbidden for themselves: they neither ride them nor taste their meat, or they reserve the meat of certain animals for men and consider it forbidden for women. And they do all this in the name of their so-called gods. We have already given the details of their such assertions in Surah al-An'am. Regarding the deities in whose names these people commit shirk, these people have no knowledge. These are their inherited notions, which have been transmitted to them from the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance). Yet these blessings have been given to them by Allah, who is One and has no partner, and regarding the deities to which they attribute these, they have no knowledge at all. In short, these are not blessings bestowed by these so-called gods; rather, these blessings belong to Allah alone, with whom these people associate partners.

Thus the clear difference between the Qur'anic view of life and the views of these ignorant people becomes evident. The Islamic belief is that all sustenance is provided by the one true God, and it should be used in His name. These people attribute some sustenance to these deities and make gods of beings from whom they have been forbidden. There is a clear difference between these two views.

But today, even with the Qur'an present and after the clarification of the doctrine of Tawhid, some people still attribute certain kinds of sustenance that Allah has provided to personalities who resemble the deities of the Jahiliyyah. Even today some people say things like, "This is the goat of Sayyid Badawi." This goat may graze wherever it likes, and no one will stop it. No one will eat it. It will be slaughtered in the name of Sayyid Badawi, and the name of Allah will not be taken over it. Some people even today vow animals in the name of certain saints and then offer these vows. These are done in the name of those saints, and the name of Allah is not taken over them; only the name of the mentioned saint is pronounced. The people of Jahiliyyah likewise offered such vows in the names of unknown gods. The eating of such animals is forbidden, even if the name of Allah is taken at the time of slaughter, because it falls under the category of what is dedicated to other than Allah (Ahl li-ghayr Allah).

Verse 56

Translation: "They swear by Allah with the strongest oaths..." Therefore this is a fabrication, and it uproots the Islamic belief and faith from its foundation. By it the root of the doctrine of Tawhid is cut. Therefore, Allah will surely call them to account concerning it.

The ideological confusion and corruption of a people regarding beliefs is not confined to the boundaries of belief alone; it penetrates the entire pattern of life and its customs and traditions. The reason is that a worldview is the single driving force behind a way of life, whether that driving force appears openly in a person's life or operates in the background.

The Arabs of the age of ignorance (Jahiliyyah) held the belief that Allah has daughters, namely that the angels are Allah's daughters. Yet their own condition was that they regarded the birth of a daughter in their homes as a very evil thing. In their view, daughters belong to Allah, while, since they prefer sons, sons belong to them.

Because of this corruption of their belief, the evil custom arose among them of burying daughters alive, or, if they kept them alive, of keeping them in extreme humiliation, mistreatment and a lowly station, and looking upon them with contempt. They thought that because of girls they would suffer disgrace and their material condition would decline, since women can neither fight wars nor earn much. Sometimes, in plunder and raids, they would take women away as captives and slave-girls, or they would become a burden on the family. Thus they would be a burden on the family's finances, and so they did not like them.

Whereas correct ideas are far removed from all of these notions. The correct belief is that provision is in the hand of Allah, and He is the Provider of all. Every person encounters only what has been written for him in his destiny. Furthermore, Allah has created man honoured, and in this man and woman are equal; moreover, without women, humanity could neither continue nor be completed, as is the command of Allah.

Here the customs of the age of ignorance are vividly portrayed.

﴿And when one of them is given the good news of a female, his face becomes dark, and he is filled with suppressed grief﴾ (16:57). That is, from sorrow and distress his face turns black, and he futilely tries to conceal his grief. He regards that birth as a calamity, whereas in reality it is a gift from Allah, just as a son is a gift, because a human being by himself can neither make a male nor create a female in the womb of the mother. Nor can a human breathe life into the foetus, nor can a human produce a living human from a simple drop. If a person reflects only on the creation of human life, on how from a drop of fluid a healthy and strong human is brought to growth, then whether the child is male or female, he would welcome it with joy. For a thinking person, every child is a miracle of Allah, and this miracle is repeated again and again; yet despite its repetition, the reality of this miracle does not diminish. The question is: if a person has sound judgement, why would he, upon receiving news of a girl's birth, grieve and hide himself from people? Because he has no hand in the creation of the girl. In this matter a father is merely a small part in the occurrence of that great miracle, and nothing more.

Now observe the wisdom of Allah, and how the miracle of life comes into being. Apparently it is seen that Allah creates a human through the union of a male and a female; just as a male is necessary for human life to come into existence, so too a female is necessary; indeed, in comparison to the male, the female is needed more, because for the nurturing of the child the woman is more essential and important, while for the man too she is a place of rest. Then why does someone's face turn black at the birth of a girl, and why does he run away from people, when he knows that the continuity of human life is impossible without women?

It is evident that deviation and corruption in thought, ideology and belief also affect customs within society and the conduct of people.

﴿Behold, how evil is their judgement﴾ (16:59). And how wrong their decisions and calculations are.

From this it becomes clear what is the importance of the Islamic worldview in correcting the collective concepts and collective ethics of human society. Furthermore, consider how great a revolution Islam has brought about in the human outlook regarding women, and how much honour it has granted to women. Not only women, but the whole of humanity has been granted honour. For in the age of ignorance it was not merely that women were humiliated; humanity itself was humiliated. Is it not evident that women are an essential element of humanity, and that to insult them is to insult humanity itself? To bury them alive is to bury humanity. Was this act not the loss of an important part of life, and a war against the wisdom of Allah's creation? The wisdom of Allah's creation is that not only man, but every living thing, is created from male and female.

Whenever humanity has deviated from correct beliefs and a correct worldview, its morals and customs have sunk into some form of jahiliyyah. Today too, despite high achievements, the world has fallen into the jahiliyyah of the twentieth century; even today the birth of a girl is not greeted with the same joy and happiness as the birth of a boy. This too is one of the customs arising from the concepts and practices of jahiliyyah. And it persists because the Islamic worldview is not clear and pure in our eyes.

It is surprising that today the worshippers of modern jahiliyyah, in hints and insinuations, raise a finger against Islamic beliefs and doctrines, saying that Islam has given women this status and that they are not free. Because of the esteem given to all humanity, women too received honour. It was declared that woman is a part of life and a part of humanity, and therefore there is no difference between the two halves of mankind, man and woman.

The Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran), Urdu translation, on Surah 16, verse 66:

Verse 66

This milk, which we extract from the udders of animals, from what is it produced? It emerges from between dung and blood. Farth (fits residue) is the term for the residue that remains in the stomach of a ruminant animal after digestion. Likewise, the solution that remains after digestion, which the intestines convert into blood, is also called farth. This blood circulates in every cell of the body. When this blood reaches the milk glands in the animal's udder, it takes on the form of milk. It is a marvel of nature that this blood becomes milk. No one knows how this solution and this blood take on the form of milk.

Then, how does the essence of every kind of food take the form of blood? Then, that from the power of this blood, the provision of nourishment to every cell of the body according to its need is a process that is extremely intricate and astonishing. This process is completed in the body every second. In this way, the process of burning also continues in the body. Every second, in this intricate machinery of the human body, the process of breakdown and building continues, and it continues for as long as the soul has not departed from the body. Any human being whose conscience is alive cannot help but be impressed by these wondrous processes, in which every particle of this strange machinery of the human body appears to be praising its Creator. This is such a strange machinery that the most complex machinery built by man has no standing in comparison with it; indeed, it is not possible for man to create even one of the countless cells of the human body.

We have given a general survey of the digestion of food in the human body, its transformation into blood, and then the process of its movement and dissolution. Such works are taking place within this body that if their scientific study and observation were carried out, the intellect would be astonished. Even the study of a single cell of the human body itself, and reflection upon it, grants thought that never ends.

Until the recent past, all these marvels remained mysteries, and this fact which the noble Qur'an mentions here, that milk emerges from between dung and blood, was unknown to man until the recent past. In earlier eras, man neither could conceive of it nor was able to study it in precise scientific detail as in our age. No person can doubt or dispute this. The clear indication of the Noble Qur'an towards one of such intricate scientific facts is itself sufficient proof that the Qur'an consists of divine revelation, because this is a fact whose scientific knowledge no human being possessed in that age.

But even if these purely scientific facts are set aside, there are still in the Qur'an proofs and distinguishing features that affirm its being divine revelation. Indeed, the emergence of one clear fact of this kind of scientific truth is sufficient to silence opponents and adversaries.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 16, verse 67:

Verse No. 67

This was in fact a preface to the ruling that was later revealed concerning the prohibition of wine. The bee acts in accordance with the inspiration that the Creator placed in its nature at the time of its creation. This too is a form of wahy (revelation), and the bee acts in accordance with it. The intricate manner in which these bees carry on their work leaves the intellect astonished. With what engineering do they build their hive? How do they divide their labour among themselves, and then how do they separate the pure honey (ʿasal muṣaffā)?

They build their homes according to their nature: in mountains, in the branches of trees, and in the climbing vines that people trellis on walls. Allah Almighty has made smooth for them, in accordance with their nature, pathways within the earth, so that this pure honey is "a cure for mankind" (shifāʾ lil-nās). Some doctors have researched this, and their research is of a highly technical nature. Yet a Muslim holds the belief that, according to this verse of the Holy Qur'an, honey is a cure for mankind. Indications of these properties of pure honey are also found in some ḥadīths of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Al-Bukhari, on the authority of Abu Saʿid al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him), reported that a man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said, "O Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), my brother has diarrhoea." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Make him drink honey." So he made him drink honey. Then he came again and said, "O Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), I made him drink honey, but his diarrhoea has only increased." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Go and make him drink honey." He went and made him drink more honey. Then he came again and said, "O Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), it has become even worse." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Allah has spoken the truth; your brother's belly is lying. So go and make him drink more honey." The man went and made his brother drink more honey, and he became well.

On reading this ḥadīth, a person is astonished at the lofty station of faith and certainty of a Messenger. The patient's brother repeatedly informs him that the illness is only increasing, yet the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prescribes the same remedy, because the Qur'an has called it a cure. In the end, the word of the Qur'an is proven true in practice. Muslims should display the same kind of faith and certainty in all those matters on which the Qur'an has given a decision, even if the apparent circumstances seem to be contrary to the command of the Qur'an. For error can occur in the observation of apparent circumstances, but Qur'anic realities can never be wrong, and in the end it is the Qur'anic realities that are proven true.

Since the subject here was drinks, in the context of cattle only milk was mentioned, because it is a drink, so that the theme and meaning would be harmonious with one another. The next lesson that follows deals, in the context of cattle (al-anʿām), also with hides, hair and wool, because there the theme is of tents and houses; therefore those products of animals that were suited to that theme and scene were mentioned there.
